{'text': 'Apple\'s first foldable iPhone is expected to be unveiled just over two weeks from now. Despite the possibility of being named the "iPhone Ultra" and a price tag exceeding $2,000, rumours suggest the device will come with several major limitations.', 'reason': None}

{'text': '#1: Telephoto Lens', 'reason': None}

{'text': 'The iPhone Ultra is reported to feature two cameras — a main lens and an ultra-wide lens — but is not expected to include a telephoto lens. For many users, this may be the biggest design drawback this time around.', 'reason': None}

{'text': 'Both the main and ultra-wide lenses on the iPhone Ultra are expected to be 48-megapixel, with specifications similar to the current base iPhone 17 model.', 'reason': None}

{'text': '#2: Action Button', 'reason': None}

{'text': "From multiple leaked iPhone Ultra dummy units, the new device will not feature an Action Button. It appears this will be the first iPhone in Apple's history to completely omit the mute switch.", 'reason': None}

{'text': 'The dummy units show the left side frame of the device to be completely blank. Reportedly, the side button and camera control button will be located on the right side frame of the iPhone Ultra, while the volume buttons will be placed on the top frame, similar to the iPad mini.', 'reason': None}

{'text': '#3: Face ID', 'reason': None}

{'text': 'The iPhone Ultra is rumoured not to feature Face ID, and instead will integrate Touch ID into the side button. This would be the first iPhone without Face ID since Apple first introduced it on the iPhone X back in 2017.', 'reason': None}

{'text': 'The reason the iPhone Ultra switches to Touch ID and drops Face ID is very likely because of the extremely thin body design; additionally, Apple would need to equip a set of Face ID components for both the outer and inner displays.', 'reason': None}

{'text': 'Apple still uses Touch ID on the power button of most iPads, including the basic iPad, iPad mini and iPad Air.', 'reason': None}

{'text': '#4: MagSafe', 'reason': None}

{'text': 'Although Apple could always surprise us, it seems the iPhone Ultra will not support MagSafe wireless charging. The back of the leaked iPhone Ultra dummy units show no MagSafe magnetic ring.', 'reason': None}

{'text': "The iPhone Ultra may, like Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 foldable phone, only offer standard wireless charging. However, based on current rumours, MagSafe seems unlikely.", 'reason': None}

{'text': '#5: Physical SIM Card', 'reason': None}

{'text': 'According to sources including Kuo Ming-Chi and Bloomberg, the iPhone Ultra will only support eSIM worldwide.', 'reason': None}

{'text': 'This arrangement is very likely related to the ultra-thin body design of the foldable iPhone. The iPhone Air has an equally slim body and is also eSIM-only worldwide; as for the iPhone 17 and iPhone 17 Pro, they currently only adopt the eSIM design in the United States and some other countries, while other markets (such as China) still retain the physical SIM card slot.', 'reason': None}

{'text': 'Summary', 'reason': None}

{'text': "It's clear that Apple's foldable iPhone Ultra will involve major trade-offs in many areas. The question is whether the practicality brought by the innovative foldable design can offset all the limitations mentioned above.", 'reason': None}

{'text': "Personally, I'm really looking forward to trying out the iPhone Ultra hands-on. The trade-off I'm most worried about is the lack of MagSafe. I'm currently using an iPhone Air, so I'm already used to living without a telephoto lens; I think I can adapt to Touch ID pretty quickly too. But my home and office are surrounded by MagSafe chargers, so switching back to regular wireless charging or being tethered to wired charging all the time will be a big change.", 'reason': None}

{'text': 'What do you think? Feel free to share your thoughts with us in the comments section.', 'reason': None}
